_note: The wardrobe: every source, race, animation and part of the layered characters, in one file. Read by scripts/art/wardrobe.mjs (checks, CREDITS.md, the render budget, the plan's tables), scripts/art/intake.mjs (one command per new asset) and scripts/art/paperdoll.mjs (a race's rules). Plan: docs/art-production-plan.md. Nothing here is a decision (D##); Michael's own words are quoted in the docs. The model files are never in the repo: <assets> is a folder outside it (see docs/art-production-plan.md), one sub-folder per source.

render._note: What every character render shares (docs/art-style.md): the cloud's processors, 256 samples, 15 pictures an animation, 8 sides, none mirrored. seconds_per_part_picture: measured 2026-11-22 by the intake on the 4-processor cloud machine, four animations of the human's 11 parts on one side (0.34 to 0.40 s for one part in one picture, the start of each run counted in; the render alone is 0.29 s).
render._gear_unit_tiles: How big a held thing from a model file is drawn: one unit of its file is this many tiles of height in a human's hand (the humans' own sizing, so a pack made to a man's measure keeps its sizes), times the race's gear_scale.
render._arms_at_rest_deg: The intake's arms check, for every race body (Michael, 2026-11-22: "Make the rest-pose alignment (forearms/hands turned to match our bones) ... standard steps of the intake tool for every new race body"): at rest, the race's forearms (elbow to wrist) and hands (wrist to knuckles, the knuckle line) may lie at most this many degrees from those of our skeleton (the file "skeleton"). Goblin Simple as it came: 16 to 32. A setting.
render._held_angle_deg: The intake's angle check, for every other race than grip_race (the grips are made on a man's hand): in every picture, a held thing may point at most this many degrees otherwise than in the grip race's hand, in the same animation and side (Michael, 2026-11-22, asked for the 'weapon angle within 5° of the human' check). Measured in the figure's own space (character.py's "pointing"); on the screen when the grip race's render is older than that. A setting.
render._shield_arm: The arm that carries a shield (proposed 2026-11-22, for Michael to approve: "Propose a shield-carrying arm pose (check UAL2 Sword_Block / Shield_OneShot first), knowing it changes the body layer"). Library 2's Idle_Shield_Loop holds the forearm across the chest, the shield up in front; Sword_Block raises the sword arm and swings the left arm back; Shield_OneShot is a bash that ends in Idle_Shield_Loop's pose. So the left arm from the shoulder down is taken from Idle_Shield_Loop at that moment (character.py --borrow) in every picture of an animation a shield is drawn in. follow: heading = it turns with the chest about the up axis and stays upright (the swing turns the body about 120 degrees in its follow-through: an arm held still ran into the chest, an arm following the chest wholly went over the head). turn: the whole arm 15 degrees up and 25 to the figure's left, at the shoulder (20 until the heater was strapped on by its own straps: then the goblin's sword met it in one picture of the swing), so the shield clears the sword and the forward thigh (found with the clipping check: 0 pictures go into anything, human and goblin, round and heater, guard and swing). The collarbone is left to the animation (it moves the neck, which belongs to the head's layer). A shield is drawn only in the animations of "in" (where a rigid arm makes sense; not in a roll, a fall, kneeling or using things: open). Such an animation has a variant, <anim>+shield, holding the shield and the parts that cover that arm ("arms": true); every other part is the plain animation's (paperdoll.mjs layerFile). All settings.

human.status: body, two tops, legs, feet, two hairs: idle and walk, facing south-east
human._slots: Also the order used when two layers are equally far from the camera, and the stacking order of --how order.
human._body: What a slot shows when nothing is worn in it: the race's own body there. This model pack's clothes replace the body under them, so a top takes the place of the bare chest and arms. Bare legs and feet are not rendered yet.
human._dressed: Only for the comparison `paperdoll.mjs orders`: the dressed body that parts are cut by when stacking is tried the plain way.
human._outfit: The dressed body a new part is tried on and lit among (a part in a slot the outfit fills takes that one's place). Also the body that parts are cut by in `paperdoll.mjs orders`.
human._ramps: The channels a layer pixel can name, in this order (ramps of scripts/art/style.mjs).
human._channels: Which of a character's own colours fills each channel when it is drawn: its skin, its hair, the dye of what it wears. null: always the ramp itself.
human._colours: The ramps each of those may take. Examples from the ramps that exist today; which colours people, hair and cloth come in is not decided.

render._note: What every render of this race is given. The files are loaded in this order every time, so the objects keep their names (the body is loaded twice: a head and a bare chest, each masked by --keep).

goblin.status: body: one idle picture at full quality, idle and walk as a trial, facing south-east
goblin._slots: "over" is new: the goblin's waistcoat goes over its shirt, so a top alone is not enough (not decided).
goblin._body: The body is always there and is one layer: the skin with its eyes, fangs and claws, and the model's own shorts, rope belt (with its small sheath and pouch) and boots, which are the goblin's underwear (Michael, 2026-11-21). The model has no hips, thighs or feet under them, so they cannot come off. Every other piece of clothing is its own layer and lies ON the body: where it is nearer to the camera it shows, as the depth in each layer pixel decides. Nothing replaces the body, unlike the human's clothes.
goblin._gear_scale: Weapons scale with the body (D121), but not as far down as its height: 0.5 (half a human, as it stands) made the blade thin in its fist and broke it into dots when it pointed at the camera. Michael, 2026-11-22, after seeing 0.5 and 0.65 side by side: "goblin sword at 0.65". A setting.
goblin._colours: Michael, 2026-11-21, 8:43 PM: "Keep every skin colour as a variant ramp (grey-teal, the greens, all of them); I'll choose defaults later." A skin is a colour filled in when the goblin is drawn: every skin ramp has five tones, and a layer pixel holds the tone's place, not the colour (ramps whose tones are not equally light pick a neighbouring tone here and there: to be matched when the default is chosen).

render._note: --ground: its boots are longer than the foot the library's animations were made for. --mask: its eyes, fangs and claws are painted into the skin's texture. --exact-ids: it has only two materials. --sized-by: its size pinned at what the body alone gives (measured 2026-11-23), so a part reaching above its head (a helmet) does not shrink everything else.
render._fit: The model as it came has another skeleton (Mixamo's): scripts/art/onto_our_rig.py puts it on ours, once ("drop": the backdrop and a sphere that came in the file). The intake makes "to" again when it is missing. Since 2026-11-22 its forearms and hands are turned, at rest, to lie as ours do (they were 16 to 18 degrees off, the hands about 30 degrees turned and drooping, so its wrist turned otherwise than the human's in every animation and it held weapons askew).

animations._note: What the game needs, read from docs/decisions.md and the game's code (the game plays Idle and Walk today), and where each comes from. action: its name in the source's file. need: slice (the first playable game), later, or never. for: null for every character and every part; or the weapon families whose held things are rendered in it (a bow is not rendered in a sword's swing; the body and the clothes are in every one). made: the sides that exist as pictures, race by race.

idle.why: Standing (the game's Idle). Approved for the Peasant as idle_alert; a relaxed idle is still to be found.

walk.why: Walking (D226). Open: the game walks a tile in 0.60 s, this walk in 1.57 s.

run.why: Running, a tile in 0.30 s (D226, D228). Sprint_Loop is the other candidate.

hit.why: Taking a hit (D161, D163: TakeDamage). Hit_Head is a second one.

dodge.why: A dodged attack (D162, D163: Rolling or Slide).

death.why: Dying; its last picture is the corpse, which stays in the world (D3).

use.why: Opening a chest or a door, taking from a corpse (D2, D232). PickUp_Table is a second one.

bandage.why: The bandage, 4 seconds (D164, D169). A stand-in: the library has no bandaging.

talk.why: Asking an NPC, NPCs talking to each other (D23).

punch.why: Unarmed attack (D171). Punch_Cross is a second one.

guard.why: Standing with a weapon drawn, in a fight (D17: attacks repeat on their own, so a fighter waits between them). Michael, 2026-11-22: "angle the blade slightly up and forward (ready stance, not pointing at the ground)". The library's Sword_Idle holds the sword hand back behind the hip (a sideways stance), so a blade raised forward from it passes into the body or hides behind the arm; and the second library's strikes start from, and end in, the plain idle's pose, not Sword_Idle's. So the guard is the plain idle with the wrist cocked 53 degrees (--add): the blade points forward and 55 degrees up, in front of the body, and the swing follows on from it. Michael, 2026-11-22, 1:18 AM: "keep the idle-based guard instead of Sword_Idle. Base it on idle_alert (the combat idle), not idle_relaxed." It is: idle_alert is the library's Idle_Loop as it is (docs/art-style.md), the action above.

swing.why: A full swing: sword, axe, mace (D224: Attack1). Michael, 2026-11-22: "Pick: attack 1 (UAL2 Sword_Regular_A + A_Rec) as the one-handed swing", in place of the first library's Sword_Attack (a hop and a deep lunge: "The attack looks weird"). The strike (0.43 s) and its recovery (0.97 s) played one after the other, from the sword stance back to it.

swing_run.why: A chaser hits a runner (D170). Not needed if the normal swing is played on the move, which D170 allows; legs that run under a swing would be a new animation, mixed from two.

dash.why: A lunging strike, 1.57 s, from the sword stance back to it. Michael, 2026-11-22: "Keep Combo, Dash and Block in the animation list for later mechanics".

combo.why: Three strikes in a row (A, B, C), 3.0 s, from the sword stance back to it. B starts where A ends and C where B ends, so B and C cannot be played alone. Kept for later mechanics (Michael, 2026-11-22).

sword_block.why: Raising the sword to block, 1.23 s, from the stance back to it. Michael, 2026-11-22: kept for later mechanics, "render Block too". Not the block of D207 (a white flash and a sound, no animation): that row stays as it is.

thrust.why: The spear's lunge, point leading (D224: Attack6). Michael, 2026-11-22: "no thrust or two-handed attacks in UAL1/UAL2; plan Mixamo for spear and greatsword later."

swing_two.why: A slow, heavy two-handed swing (D171), the greatsword's. Neither library has one (Sword_Heavy_Combo of the second is one-handed): Mixamo, later (Michael, 2026-11-22).

shoot.why: Drawing and loosing a bow (D171). Neither library has one (the first has a pistol).

asleep.why: Lying asleep: a newcomer in the waking place (D71). Not for a player who has left: that character leaves the world (D49). LayToIdle of the second library starts lying and gets up: its first picture is the sleeper, the rest the waking.

sneak.why: Stealth, after the slice (D151). With Crouch_Idle_Loop.

sit.why: Sitting, with Sitting_Enter, Sitting_Exit and Sitting_Talking_Loop.

cast.why: Magic, after the slice (D24, D151). With Spell_Simple_Enter, _Idle_Loop and _Exit.

swim.why: No swimming in the first game (D102).

work.why: Trades, once crafting is in (D141). The second library has TreeChopping_Loop, Farm_Harvest, Farm_PlantSeed, Farm_Watering; no hammering, no fishing.

ride.why: Riding a mount. Neither library says it has it; not looked for yet.

block.why: A block is a white flash and a sound, no animation (D207).

families._note: Weapon families: which animations a held thing is rendered in, beside the ones every part is in. From D171 (unarmed, one-handed, two-handed, bows) and D224 (the spear thrusts). hold: how it sits in the hand (scripts/art/held_gear.py).

two_handed.hold: fist, the off hand on the grip too (not built)

bow.hold: in the off hand, upright (not built)

shield.hold: strapped on the forearm: a strap near the elbow, the fist round a handle (held_gear.py), carried up in front (render.shield_arm)

parts._note: Every part. kind: body, clothing, hair, weapon or shield. races: who wears it (clothes, armour and hair are per race; weapons and shields are shared, rendered once per race on that race's hands: "all"). meshes: the objects of the race's loaded files that make it up; or file + hold for a held thing from its own model file. materials: which ramps each of its materials may take. status: trial (not approved), approved, or stand-in.
